status_summary: USTR released a WTO reform paper on 2026-03-23 (WT/GC/W/998), building on a December 2025 paper, that proposes members agree on objective criteria for who may use special and differential treatment, pointing to the 2019 US draft criteria (OECD members or applicants, G20 members, high-income economies and members with at least 0.5 percent of world merchandise trade) as an indicative approach; the paper says China's September 2025 pledge raises questions and that there should never be another WTO agreement in which China is eligible for such treatment. China announced on 2025-09-23 that it would not seek new special and differential treatment in WTO negotiations while keeping its developing-country status, a decision by China rather than a US action. China's self-declared status has not changed, and no WTO decision on eligibility criteria was found. H.Res. 687, a non-binding House resolution introduced 2025-09-09 stating that China should no longer be classified as a developing country by the UN, was referred to the House Foreign Affairs Committee with no later action.

timeline.event: H.Res. 687, stating that China should no longer be classified as a developing country by the UN, was introduced and referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs; no later action is recorded.

USTR issued a paper on WTO reform, the first of two reform papers listed on its WTO reform page.

Other international bodies (UN, World Bank) were not searched beyond that resolution. China's pledge is a Chinese decision, not a US action, and does not set the stage.
